newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms, heating oil cargo premiums rise.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms, heating oil cargo premiums rise.

text.p: NWE heating oil cargo premiums firmed slightly on Monday on improved demand while those for low sulphur diesel cargoes were under pressure, traders said.

Prices rose on IPE November futures, which finished up $2.75 at $227.00 a tonne in line with Brent crude futures. Brent futures were boosted by news of heavy buying of gasoline on the U.S. Gulf coast. Gas oil physical trade was thin, traders said.
Traders said several trans-Atlanic cargoes weighed on winter grade low sulphur diesel premiums while buying interest for heating oil had quickened on a perception of tightened supply.
"Diesel cargoes are now well-supplied," one trader said.
Premiums for cargoes of refinery grade heating oil for early November delivery rose to a notional Nov IPE +$3.50/5.00 from 1.25/2.25 heard on Friday.

Russian was bid into Britain at Nov IPE +$4 and offered at $5.50, $2 firmer. Diesel cargoes earlier rose to a notional Nov +26, following a trade at that level on Friday, from +$23/24. On barges, heating oil refinery grade was around Nov IPE +$0.50/1.00 for late October and +$1.00/1.50 for early November. Low sulphur diesel (-7/-22) was offered slightly easier at Nov IPE +$31/33 for early November with bids at +$25/26.
